page.layout: One page of running text in a single column; margin notes in the right margin: "Magistratus pericula." beside the first lines, and a group of notes beside the lower lines. Printed page number 213 at the top right; running head at the top centre; signature at the foot.

main_text.p: Tu ergo nunciterum vide, Annon perhoc Iefuitarum decretum omnium Europaeorum Regum & quorumcunq; Magistratuum Politicorum mors & vita ab arbitrio Iefuitici horoscopo suspendatur? Vt si hic illis dextrè ascenMagistratus pericula.dat, ipsi viuant & valeant, sin minus, pereant? Qua de re prædicta Venerorum calamitas, Regis Britanniæ perpetua pericula, & illorum omnium metus, qui hunc Ordinem sibi infestū sentiunt, abundè testantur. Venetorum tamen exemplum præcipuè confpicuum est, quòd Respub. illa, vt dixi, Romano-Catholicam religionem hactenus, tanquam Imperii sui Palladium, accuratè obseruet & acerrimè tueatur.

Quæ exempla quoties expendo, toties exhorresco, cùm vid£ am quàm facilè sub præsenti rerum statu inter nos simile quiddam in alterutram partem accidere possit, postquam inprimis Gentis Iefuiticæ ad huiusmodi aliquem effectum tam pertinaces & feruidi conatus ab aliquot iam annis inter nos deprehenduntur.

Sed heic fortassis dicere voles, Inter nos nihil ab hac parte esse periculi, quòd Iefuitis cum Rege nostro probè conueniat, &c. Mallem te dicere posse, Regi nostro cum Regni ordinibus & his cum regia Maiestate probè conuenire.

Hoc enim ad Reipub. salutem aliquanto vtilius, & ad securitatem nostram firmius & effiRegis vita & fortunæ ab hac pendet, de Regni fortunis Iefuitarum affectus obnoxia.cacius esset. Nunc autem hoc ab ste verè dici agnosco, neq; tamen hoc ipsum follicitudinis meæ caussam tollit, sed eandem potiùs auget.

page.notes: Right-margin notes are printed in small italic type and run together across lines; the notes beside the lower lines are partly obscured and read with doubt. The marginal note "Regis vita & fortunæ ab hac pendet..." is a best reading. "Venerorum" (first line) is uncertain and may be "Venetorum". "vid£ am" and "dicere voles" are doubtful print. The line "Cacius esset" is printed "cacius esset". The cut-off at the foot of the lower lines (line ends "effi-" / "cacius") is read as printed. The word "aliquanto" is clearly printed. The outlined middle-foot mark is not a numbered note.
